chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Whoever washes his hands before the meal and after it, he will live in ease and be cured of affliction in his body.
ai.seo_question: What are the benefits of washing hands before and after eating according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) links physical hygiene to divine protection, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the interconnection between bodily purity and spiritual well-being. The promise of 'ease' (saa'ah) suggests not only material comfort but also a broadened scope for worship and daily activities, while protection from 'affliction' (balwa) underscores the holistic view of health in Islamic tradition.
